notes: Canonical memory-comparison SQL/data/parameters and batch counts; diagnostic, not a cross-core benchmark.
All timing precedes tracing. Allocation tracing disables GC for one query at a time; traced time is never reported.
Core allocation sites exclude Ruby internal objects. Answer digests compare query and execute paths on the first parameter.

results.sql: SELECT score FROM items WHERE id = $1
SELECT a.label, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id LIMIT 1
SELECT a.label, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id LIMIT 1
SELECT a.id, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id < $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id + 1 AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id
SELECT a.id, b.score FROM items a LEFT JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id AND b.bucket <> 3 WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
SELECT a.id, b.id, b.score FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.bucket = a.bucket AND b.score <> a.score WHERE a.id = $1 ORDER BY b.id
SELECT a.id, b.score, c.label FROM items a JOIN items b ON b.id = a.id JOIN items c ON c.id = b.id WHERE a.id = $1 AND b.id = $1 AND c.id = $1 ORDER BY a.id
